title: Xanthe and the Lantern
premise: Coral Delacroix carries sealed dispatches for the Republic of Vessany's final envoy, racing winter to the river fortress of Xanthe where a last treaty might be signed. When the season's first ice closes the bridge, she is trapped inside walls already splitting between loyalists and the general who will soon sell the republic to save himself. Reading the dispatches she was never meant to open, Coral discovers the envoy's mission is not peace but surrender, and that her own family's name is on the list of those to be given up. She must choose between loyalty to the man who raised her and the truth owed to the people about to be erased, smuggling the real record out through the besieged city before the river thaws and the victors' historians arrive to write it otherwise. The book ends with Coral crossing the breaking ice with the true account in hand, the republic lost but its record surviving.
about_author: P. M. Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private papers of displaced governments in exile. They write historical fiction about the clerks, couriers, and record-keepers whom official histories forget.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Coral Delacroix, courier to the dying Republic of Vessany, weighs her dispatch case against her life's few possessions as she prepares to ride east. In her POV, we learn she measures everything by what fits in a satchel. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: The Envoy's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Coral delivers sealed orders to Ambassador Ilan Voss, her guardian since childhood, who is unusually tender and evasive. His POV alternates briefly, hinting he knows more than he says. Beat: love shadowed by concealment.

chapters.title: Road to Xanthe
chapters.summary: On the road, Coral passes refugee columns fleeing the advancing coalition armies and hears first rumors of negotiations at the fortress city of Xanthe. Her POV; she begins questioning what the dispatches contain. Beat: unease hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Coral reaches the bridge over the River Sarn just as garrison engineers close it for the season, ice jamming the pilings. Trapped outside the walls overnight, she witnesses deserters turned away. Her POV. Beat: the world narrowing to one frozen crossing.

chapters.title: Inside the Walls
chapters.summary: Admitted at last, Coral enters Xanthe: ration lines, factional salutes, General Aurec Maren's soldiers everywhere. She meets Sergeant Teyo Brandt, a cynical garrison veteran who becomes her reluctant ally. Her POV. Beat: claustrophobia and wary connection.

chapters.title: The Sealed Room
chapters.summary: Coral catalogs the embassy's papers and notices a second set of dispatches, ciphered differently, that bypass her entirely. Her POV, with growing archival instinct. Beat: the archivist's itch — something is being hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: General Maren's Dinner
chapters.summary: At a tense banquet, Maren charms the envoy while his aide probes Coral about the republic's remaining assets. Coral performs loyalty while measuring exits. Her POV. Beat: power's seduction observed up close.

chapters.title: Teyo's War
chapters.summary: Teyo Brandt's POV chapter: his history with Maren, the men he's lost, and why he stays loyal to the garrison rather than the general. He warns Coral that Xanthe will be traded away. Beat: disillusioned devotion.

chapters.title: Breaking the Cipher
chapters.summary: Working nights, Coral cracks the secondary cipher using her mother's old merchant code. She reads the first decoded line: names — including her own family — listed under 'surrender terms.' Her POV. Beat: cold shock.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Coral confronts Voss privately; he admits the mission is capitulation dressed as treaty, insisting it saves lives. Their argument splits the book's moral core. Alternating POV. Beat: heartbreak — both are right.

chapters.title: The Historian Arrives
chapters.summary: Coalition envoy and court historian Sereth Olland arrives under flag of truce, already drafting the official narrative of Vessany's 'orderly dissolution.' Coral watches him flatter Maren. Her POV. Beat: horror at history being written in advance.

chapters.title: The Lantern
chapters.summary: Coral recalls her father's lantern, left with her as a child — inside its base, a hollow for documents. She realizes the archive she keeps could become the counter-record. Her POV. Beat: purpose igniting.

chapters.title: Copies by Candlelight
chapters.summary: With Teyo guarding the door, Coral copies the surrender lists and forged casualty ledgers that hide a planned massacre of republican officials. Teyo's POV. Beat: complicity becoming courage.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive
chapters.summary: A junior clerk discovers the copying and reports it — not to Voss, but to Maren's aide. Coral barely escapes arrest; Voss covers for her at terrible cost. Her POV. Beat: paranoia and gratitude entangled.

chapters.title: Maren's Offer
chapters.summary: Maren summons Coral alone and offers her a place in the new order — safety, rank, her family spared — if she surrenders the originals and testifies to Voss's treason. Her POV. Beat: temptation laid bare.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Coral refuses, telling Maren that records outlive regimes. Maren orders the archive sealed and the bridge guarded against thaw. Teyo arranges a route across the ice instead. Mixed POV. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss, exposed and disgraced, gives Coral his personal testimony and blesses her mission, choosing truth over the fiction they both served. His final POV chapter. Beat: redemption purchased with ruin.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Ice
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Coral and Teyo slip the lantern-laden sledge onto the frozen river under searchlights and gunfire as Maren signs the surrender. Dual POV. Beat: terror and resolve.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Mid-river, the ice fractures; Teyo goes down saving the sledge, and Coral loses the lantern — then finds it wedged downstream, contents dry. Her POV. Beat: grief and miracle in one breath.

chapters.title: The Other Shore
chapters.summary: Coral reaches the far bank into coalition territory, is detained by Sereth Olland's staff, and gambles everything by handing Olland the true record alongside his own false draft. Her POV. Beat: high-stakes persuasion.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Olland, confronted with evidence his patron ordered the massacre, quietly amends the official history — the victors' historian becomes the record's unlikely custodian. Olland's POV. Beat: ambiguous justice.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring: Coral files the lantern's documents in an exile archive, visits Teyo's grave on the Sarn's bank, and writes the first line of her own account. Her POV. Beat: mourning transmuted into memory — belonging found in bearing witness.
